newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault to sell parts for Iranian car.
newsitem.headline: Renault to sell parts for Iranian car.

text.p: France's Renault said on Monday it had signed an agreement with an Iranian carmaker to deliver mechanical parts for a new multi-purpose vehicle scheduled to go into production in 1998 at a car plant in the Gulf island of Kish, developed by Iran as an export-oriented duty-free zone.

Renault said in a statement that the agreement entailed the delivery of parts to Kish Khodro company from the Megane car collection, including 1.6 litre engines and gear boxes. The terms were not disclosed.

Kish Khodro is 51 percent held by private Iranian investors, 40 percent held by an Iranian state bank, with the rest of the capital in the hands of a British engineering group, BMS Management, which designed the MPV, Renault said.

Kish Khodro is scheduled to start building an assembly plant this month on Kish, with production set to begin in mid-1998. Production is expected to reach 5,000 vehicles annually for domestic consumption and export.
